introduction: New Hampshire WIC applications begin online or by contacting a local clinic for an appointment. The clinic completes the assessment and explains food and nutrition benefits.
description: New Hampshire WIC applications begin online or by contacting a local clinic for an appointment. The clinic completes the assessment and explains food and nutrition benefits.

sections.who: New Hampshire WIC serves pregnant applicants, breastfeeding parents through the baby’s first year, non-breastfeeding parents through six months after birth, and children younger than five. Applicants must live in their local agency’s service area, meet income rules and have a nutrition risk assessed by WIC staff. The state publishes income guidelines at 185% of the federal poverty level; use its current household-size table rather than an older dollar limit.
sections.get: Benefits support nutrition through approved foods, education, breastfeeding support and referrals. They are different from a general food-budget EBT award.
sections.docs:

sections.apply:
1. Choose a clinic

    Find your local clinic through SignUpWIC or call 800-942-4321.

  2. Request an appointment

    The NH WIC pre-application lets you select a town and clinic to call you. If transferring from another state, call instead of submitting this pre-application.

  3. Complete certification

    Ask the clinic which documents and family members to bring. Staff complete the eligibility and nutrition assessment and explain your food benefits.
sections.after: Keep appointment instructions and contact the clinic about replacement cards or benefit changes. For account and benefit information, customer support is 855-279-0680; ebtEDGE also provides account access. If you disagree with an eligibility decision, ask about the state’s WIC fair-hearing process.
sections.sources: Reviewed October 1, 2026 using NH WIC application and shopping guidance, NH WIC eligibility and the NH identity policy. USA Assistance background guide.

faqs: Yes. Use the NH WIC pre-application to request a clinic appointment; it does not complete certification.
Is a Social Security card the only acceptable identity proof?
No. NH’s published identity policy lists several alternatives; confirm the appropriate record with the clinic.
No. The clinic completes the eligibility and nutrition assessment.
What if I already receive WIC in another state?
Call the New Hampshire WIC office to arrange a transfer. The state says not to use the online pre-application for transfers.
Contact your local WIC clinic for a replacement card or changes to your food benefits.
